speaker: Patient
text: 1-month-old boy. The patient’s mother reports that the infant occasionally stops breathing while sleeping, with episodes increasing in frequency. The patient was born prematurely at 32 weeks due to placental insufficiency and required respiratory support immediately post-birth. Prenatal testing indicated the mother was not immune to rubella. speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Tetralogy of Fallot (TOF) with Eisenmenger syndrome or a left-to-right shunt lesion (e.g., VSD) causing pulmonary overcirculation and subsequent apnea/anemia.

REQUEST TEST: Echocardiogram
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential
REQUEST TEST: Arterial Blood Gas (ABG)

The infant's history of prematurity, placental insufficiency, maternal rubella exposure, and family history of heart disease raises concern for congenital heart defects. The episodes of apnea and anemia could be secondary to cyanotic spells (tet spells) or polycythemia-related complications from chronic hypoxia. An echocardiogram is essential to confirm the diagnosis.
